author: TIMOTHY A. FARWELL
title: Pickleball excuses: A guide to dodging blame with style - NewsBreak
text: Let’s be honest — pickleball is not just a sport. It’s a theater of triumph, tragedy and Oscar-worthy performances of denial. Sure, some folks own up when they whiff the ball like they are playing ghost pickleball. But some have fragile egos. That's why it's important to have an excuse waiting backstage, ready to jump out there. However, if you ever find yourself needing a graceful way to explain why your paddle suddenly turned into a baguette at match point, fear not. I’ve compiled the ultimate list of excuses to help you maintain your pride and pin the blame on anything but your coordination. Act I: The Classic Deflections "I wasn’t ready." Ah yes, the timeless masterpiece. You stand there, eyes open, paddle up, game in progress, but, nope, you were emotionally unprepared for that shot. They can’t argue with that. What are they gonna do, peek inside your soul? Imagine what must dwell deep inside the pickleball mind. "The sun was in my eyes." This excuse is so common that it's hard to sell. Also, it's very limiting since it's only usable when you’re actually facing the sun. If it's nighttime, just switch it around and say, "The lights aren't bright enough for me." Did you get the "for me?" No one can dispute it. "I thought YOU were going to get it." Excellent for stirring up teammate tension. Say this quickly, before your partner can use it on you. It's like a game within the game. If they beat you to it, whip out the rebuttal: “It was closer to you.” Is it true? Doesn’t matter. Say it with enough conviction and they’ll doubt their own memory. Act II: The Optical Illusions "I didn’t think it was coming over." This one’s great if the ball barely clears the net. Say it enough times and people will start believing you or they may think you have an uncanny knack for misjudging basic physics. "You jinxed me." Perfect for situations where your partner says something encouraging like, “We’ve got this.” Bam — instant hex. Put them on mute next round just in case. "The ball isn’t yellow enough." Is it neon? Mustard? Lemon chiffon? Doesn’t matter. If you’re feeling bold, argue about the exact Pantone shade. Get them to wonder if they brought the wrong equipment or just displeased the pickleball gods. Act III: Psychological Warfare "My paddle is too stiff." Sure, it’s the same paddle you’ve used all year. But today? It’s a rebel. It’s got attitude. Or maybe it’s auditioning for a role in a martial arts flick. "My shoes are too big." This gem works best if your shoes fit perfectly. The goal is confusion. If you’re slipping, it’s because you’ve entered clown mode. Honk your nose for emphasis. "The shot was too easy." This is the pretentious art critic of excuses. You missed because it was beneath you. Like someone asking Picasso to draw a stick figure. Act IV: Chaos and Calamity "I lost my forehand." Casually claim your forehand wandered off sometime between warm-up and now. Did it go to brunch without you? Is it sulking in your sock drawer? Keep the mystery alive. "I don’t know how I missed it." This isn’t just an excuse — it’s a philosophical cry for help. Shrug your shoulders, gaze at the sky and imply that there are cosmic forces working against you. Ideally, someone will offer to burn some sage to chase away the evil pickleball demons. Bonus Round: Wild Cards "There was a dog." Was there really a dog? Who cares. Mention it and at least one person will look around in mild panic. If there was a dog, congratulate yourself on excellent observational skills. "Someone’s grilling burgers." You're not distracted — you’re hungry. Let your opponent's know that unless they plan to feed you mid-match, you can’t be expected to perform. "I was protecting nature." Saw a bug crawling across the baseline? You hesitated to step on it. The ball may be out, but your conscience is clear. Pickleball isn’t just volleys and footwork — it’s about crafting an experience. So next time you miss a shot, don’t let reality ruin your reputation. Call on one of these classic excuses, delivered with confidence, flair and maybe a touch of melodrama. Because deep down, we all know it wasn’t your fault.
